subject: Television & Streaming
title: Why Crime Never Leaves TV
description: A micro-lesson that makes Why Crime Never Leaves TV usable.

hook.text: Crime has been TV's dominant genre since the 1950s. Dragnet started it. The genre has never stopped growing.

buildup.text: Crime stories satisfy a deep psychological need: the desire to see order restored and wrongdoers punished.

discovery.text: Procedurals offer closure in a world that rarely provides it. Every episode ends with answers, even if reality doesn't.

twist.text: Modern crime shows like Mindhunter complicate that comfort. Sometimes there's no justice—just understanding.

climax.text: Crime TV endures because it addresses the most basic human fear: that bad things happen and nobody is held accountable.

punchline.text: We watch crime shows to believe justice is possible.

quiz.question: What psychological need do crime procedurals primarily satisfy?
options: The need to see order restored and wrongdoers punished
